milestone: Operator directive: repo-weight invariant breach flagged (total tracked bytes ~115.5MB against a ~103MB budget); triage, find the actual offending path(s) via git history, and either relocate/delete dense material per CLAUDE.md's Dense Materials rule or produce an itemized report for operator judgment — never raise the budget or extend the FROZEN grandfather list. Closes the unresolved risk named in RES-2026-08-23-REPO-WEIGHT-PREEXISTING-HEADROOM-001 ('identify and relocate a grandfathered or newly-oversized tracked file... as its own repository-hygiene task').
problem: `tests/repo-weight.test.ts`'s total-tracked-bytes canary failed: the repo carried 116,395,201 bytes (111.0 MB) against the 103,000,000-byte (98 MB) MAX_TRACKED_TOTAL_BYTES budget, ~13.4 MB over.
observedFailure: `npx vitest run tests/repo-weight.test.ts` reported 'the repo now carries 111.0 MB of tracked files, over the 98 MB budget' at branch tip 77b7f99ee.

The per-file oversize check ('no NEW tracked file exceeds 1MB') was PASSING throughout — no single new file over 1MB caused this. The overage was the aggregate of ~2,322 newly tracked files (mostly legitimate source/tests/docs added over ~1,836 commits since the budget was last frozen on 2026-08-02) plus organic growth in existing files, minus some removed files — genuine, distributed codebase growth with no single smoking-gun commit.
rootCauses: Within that distributed growth, one identifiable, non-organic block of dense material was hiding in plain sight: `design-assets/metaMe/{sources,iQube}/**` (45 files, 19.4 MB of PNG/EPS/AI/CDR brand renders and derivative icon-size ladders). `git grep -r design-assets` across the entire repo (application code, config, tests) matched only `tests/repo-weight.test.ts` itself (the grandfather-list entries) and one prose doc recording its own history — zero import/src/fetch/require references anywhere.

This material was NOT newly added by any recent session. It originated from a 2026-09-07 Amplify BUILD-ARTIFACT-size incident (see codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-09-07_amplify-build-size-cap-incident-and-handoff.md), which relocated `public/metaMe/sources/` and `public/metaMe/iQube/` (~20MB, 'verified zero code references') OUT of `public/` and into `design-assets/metaMe/` to stop those bytes from being traced into the Next.js deploy artifact. That fix was correct and effective FOR THE PROBLEM IT SOLVED (the Amplify SSR-Compute artifact-size cap, governed by `.next/standalone` weight per the separate Amplify Build-Size Budget section of CLAUDE.md) — but a relocation from one in-repo path to another in-repo path does not remove a single byte from `git ls-files`, which is what `tests/repo-weight.test.ts`'s DIFFERENT budget (repository tracked-tree weight) measures. The 2026-09-07 fix's own grandfather-list entry (6 of the 45 files) even said so explicitly at the time: 'still grandfathered debt, now at least not costing every Amplify build its size budget' — correctly scoped to the artifact-size problem, silent on the repo-weight one. The other 36 files (the per-colorway icon-size-ladder derivatives under `iQube/`) were never individually over 1MB, so they were never grandfathered or flagged by the per-file check at all, and simply rode along as untracked debt until the aggregate total-budget canary caught it here.

This is the same repository-hygiene defect flagged as an unresolved risk in RES-2026-08-23-REPO-WEIGHT-PREEXISTING-HEADROOM-001 ('the pre-existing headroom is effectively exhausted... this should be triaged as its own repository-hygiene task') — that record explicitly declined to fix it inline and asked for a dedicated pass, which this resolution is.
resolution: Confirmed via `npx vitest run tests/repo-weight.test.ts` the exact failing measurement (116,395,201 bytes vs the 103,000,000-byte budget) before making any change.

Diffed tracked-file sizes between the commit that last froze the budget (e1240c6f0, 2026-08-02, repo at 93.25MB) and HEAD (111.0MB) via `git ls-tree -r -l` at both commits, confirming no single new file over 1MB was the cause (2,322 new files totaling 39.2MB, 111 removed files totaling 24.4MB, plus growth in existing files — organic, distributed growth) before searching for a non-organic block within that growth.

Identified `design-assets/metaMe/{sources,iQube}/**` (45 files, 19.4MB) as confirmed-zero-code-reference dead weight via a repo-wide grep for `design-assets` (zero application-code matches) and cross-referenced against the 2026-09-07 incident doc's own prior 'verified zero code references' finding for the same material.

Before removal: computed a sha256 manifest of all 45 files and copied their bytes into this session's scratchpad, so the exact original content remains verifiable/recoverable independent of git history alone.

Removed all 45 files from git tracking (`git rm -r design-assets/metaMe/iQube design-assets/metaMe/sources`) — left the small (8.7KB) `design-assets/metaMe/CONSTITUTIONAL_BRAND_ASSETS.md` registry doc untouched in place, since it is prose documentation (provenance/usage rules), not dense binary material, and CLAUDE.md's Dense Materials section explicitly allows 'a JSON or Markdown record with the CID or storage path, title, hash, provenance' to be committed.

Retired the 6 now-nonexistent GRANDFATHERED_OVERSIZE entries in `tests/repo-weight.test.ts` (the 2026-09-07 entries for the `sources/*` files), replacing them with a dated retirement comment naming what was removed, why, and where the bytes + sha256 manifest are preserved pending upload — following the file's own established retirement-comment pattern (see the 2026-08-15 `artifacts/build-info/...` retirement comment already in that file). Per CLAUDE.md's own text ('Deleting or relocating a grandfathered file needs no permission and no bookkeeping... tidying the list afterwards is welcome, not required'), this required no operator sign-off.
Did NOT touch MAX_TRACKED_TOTAL_BYTES (kept at 103,000,000) and did NOT add any new grandfathered entry.

Verified `npx vitest run tests/repo-weight.test.ts` after the change: repo weight now 96,026,077 bytes (91.6MB), comfortably under the 103,000,000-byte budget (~6.4MB of real headroom) — all four `repo weight` describe-block assertions pass, plus the pre-existing `a grandfathered entry cannot outlive the debt it describes` and `the budget is re-frozen...` assertions.

Confirmed via `git diff --stat` against the base commit (77b7f99ee) that exactly 46 files changed (45 deleted design assets + the test file edit) and via `git status --short | grep` that zero paths under services/vela/, services/factor/, services/moneypenny/, app/(shell)/moneypenny/, or app/api/moneypenny/ were touched, per the operator's explicit scope boundary (concurrent, unrelated Vela Use Case Zero work in progress on other sessions).
rejectedApproaches: Raising MAX_TRACKED_TOTAL_BYTES to make the failure disappear — rejected per CLAUDE.md's explicit text: 'Raising this number is not the fix.'

Adding a new GRANDFATHERED_OVERSIZE entry for any of the 45 files — rejected: the rule is 'an entry may be REMOVED... never added,' and in any case only 6 of the 45 were ever individually over the 1MB per-file threshold, so a grandfather-list entry would not even have been the mechanism that fixed the total-budget failure.

Deleting the manuscript directory `codexes/packs/polity-core/items/commentary/constitutional-internet/` (2.3MB of book chapter drafts, a genuine Dense-Materials-rule violation category per CLAUDE.md's explicit 'Manuscripts and long-form work — chapter drafts, book builds, exports' prohibition) or the `docs/qubetalk-bridge/outbox/` accumulation (0.62MB of transient bridge packets) as additional budget headroom — rejected as unnecessary once the design-assets/metaMe removal alone cleared the budget with margin, and because both require operator judgment on canonical destination (working draft -> Supabase vs. ratified/frozen -> Auto Drive) that this task's own instructions reserve for the operator rather than an agent guess. Flagged in the accompanying update doc as a secondary, non-blocking observation instead.

Actually uploading the removed files to Supabase Storage myself before deleting them from git — rejected: this session has no verified live Supabase Storage upload path (no MCP storage-upload tool, and per CLAUDE.md's 'Session Start — Verify Connector/MCP Access' rule, connector reachability must be verified, never assumed; even a reachable Supabase MCP here only exposes SQL/migration tools, not a blob-storage upload primitive). Fabricating a storage URL would violate CLAUDE.md's No-Guessing rule. Instead: original bytes + sha256 manifest preserved in the session scratchpad and named in the update doc for the operator to complete the actual upload, with the git history itself (parent commit) as a secondary recovery path in the interim.
unresolvedRisks: codexes/packs/polity-core/items/commentary/constitutional-internet/ (2.3MB, book chapter drafts) is a genuine Dense-Materials-rule violation candidate (CLAUDE.md explicitly names 'Manuscripts and long-form work — chapter drafts, book builds, exports' as never-commit material) that was NOT touched here because it did not block the budget and its canonical destination (Supabase working-draft vs. Auto Drive ratified-CID) needs operator judgment. Left for a future dedicated pass or explicit operator instruction.

docs/qubetalk-bridge/outbox/ (0.62MB across 28 files) is a growing, never-pruned accumulation of transient fire-and-forget bridge packets (CLAUDE.md's own bridge doc describes them as ephemeral relay payloads, not a permanent record) that will keep growing every session that uses the bridge. Not touched here (did not block the budget); a future session could add a retention/pruning policy.

The 45 removed design-asset files are recoverable via `git show <commit-before-this-resolution>:<path>` and via the sha256-verified copies preserved in this session's scratchpad, but neither is a durable, generally-accessible location. The actual Supabase Storage (or Auto Drive) upload + pointer-doc update per CLAUDE.md's Dense Materials table remains outstanding operator/future-agent work.
